title: Basic 4 · Apply a mask
summary: Circular mask: keep only the central disk of an image, replace the outside with a background value. Fundamental for particle masking.

steps.title: Try masking
steps.body: Masking keeps a chosen region of an image and replaces the rest with a background value. In cryo-EM it's used all the time to crop the noisy surround away from particle centres. This lesson cuts out a circular region with **Circular mask**.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph so `data.camera` shows its image before we attach the mask.

steps.title: Drop Circular mask
steps.body: From the Masking category, drag **Circular mask** (`mask.circle`).

steps.title: Wire Camera → Mask
steps.body: Drag from Camera's `image` output to Circular mask's `image` input.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. The default radius is small, so you'll see a tiny preserved disk — the baseline before you pick a sensible radius.

steps.title: Click Mask
steps.body: Click Mask. The Inspector reveals `outer_radius` (radius of the kept disk, in pixels), `inner_radius` (for an annulus — set > 0 to punch a central hole), `edge` (`disk` = hard / `cos` = soft), `edge_width`, `background_mode`, and `background`.

steps.title: Set outer_radius to 60
steps.body: Enter **60**. A disk of radius 60 is kept in the centre.

steps.title: Run the graph
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. The output has the camera image inside the radius-60 disk and the image mean (default `background_mode = average`) outside.

steps.title: 🎉 Done
steps.body: Change `edge` to `cos` for a cosine roll-off at the boundary — this suppresses ringing in Fourier space (Comparison 2 explores a similar point for filters). The Masking category also offers `mask.gaussian`, `mask.binarize`, and `mask.threshold` for other use cases. Next: **Basic 5 · Window / crop (WI)**.
